expectations.text: The reply says that in Sweden the selection follows the LAS order by length of service, unless a collective agreement or a list agreed with the union says otherwise, and that the employer may exempt up to three employees.
expectations.evidence: "in Sweden, LAS sets the order by length of service unless you agree otherwise with the union". Step 5: "the LAS order per order-of-priority group, keeping longer-serving people who are qualified for a remaining role." Step 6: "an agreed list (avtalsturlista) ... plus the three LAS exemptions with written reasons."

expectations.text: The reply says the employer must negotiate with the union under the Co-determination Act (MBL) before deciding.
expectations.evidence: Step 3: "Negotiate before deciding: open MBL negotiations with the union now, with the real numbers, while they can still change the plan." (Minor: step 2's voluntary exits and redeployment are listed before step 3, but 'now' and 'before deciding' make the timing clear.)

expectations.text: The reply rejects selecting people by tickets resolved or CSAT as the method, and explains why (the law and the metric's flaws).
expectations.evidence: "I wouldn't select on tickets resolved and CSAT: in Sweden, LAS sets the order by length of service ..., and now that AI takes the easy tickets, per-person counts would cut the people handling the hard cases." Step 7: "Never criteria: ticket counts". Both the law and the metric's flaw are covered.

expectations.text: The reply mentions the nine-month re-employment priority and support through a job security council or transition study support.
expectations.evidence: Step 8: "Support from the day of notice: TRR or your job security council, nine months' re-employment priority, transition study support."

expectations.text: The reply first checks the cut itself: whether people could be redeployed to other work (for example complex cases or new services) instead of nine dismissals.
expectations.evidence: Step 1: "Test the 9. Use measured AI quality (reopens, escalations, CSAT on AI-handled tickets), not the vendor's deflection rate." Step 2: "Shrink it first: hiring freeze, attrition, internal vacancies, voluntary exits, redeployment into second line and AI quality work."

expectations.text: The reply stays short (under about 300 words) and opens with the answer.
expectations.evidence: wc -w reply.md = 269. It opens with the answer: "I wouldn't select on tickets resolved and CSAT: in Sweden, LAS sets the order..."

factual_errors.evidence: Checked and correct: the LAS order per priority group with a qualification requirement, the agreed list (avtalsturlista), three exemptions, MBL negotiation, nine months' re-employment priority, TRR and other job security councils, transition study support (omställningsstudiestöd), and the two-month Arbetsförmedlingen notice. '9 roles (30%)' is right (9/30). The Klarna 2025 claim matches reporting.

skill_leak.evidence: No mention of a skill, reference files, 'cost ladder' or 'rungs'. 'the skills they need' refers to employee skills.

owns_result.evidence: The prompt describes a planned reduction, not a bad outcome that leadership caused.

best_insight.value: It gives HR a lawful route to its goal: an agreed list (avtalsturlista) with role-based criteria fixed before anyone is scored. It also says to test the 9 against measured AI quality rather than the vendor's deflection rate, and to stop the work that leaves with the 9.

suggestions.reason: All four samples pass all six assertions, so the set does not separate them. The differences sit in things no assertion checks: the Arbetsförmedlingen notice (two months before the first last day for 5-25 people), defining the remaining roles and their qualification needs before anyone is assessed, ruling out leave, sickness and part-time as factors, and cutting work along with roles.

suggestions.assertion: The reply stays short (under about 300 words) and opens with the answer.
suggestions.reason: Every reply is 258-270 words, so 'under about 300' doesn't discriminate. It also ignores that one sample adds a 622-word document after the user said 'Keep it short'. Consider an assertion on whether the whole hand-over respects that request, or a tighter cap.

suggestions.assertion: The reply first checks the cut itself: whether people could be redeployed to other work (for example complex cases or new services) instead of nine dismissals.
suggestions.reason: This is a compound check (question the 9, then redeploy to new work), and all samples pass it easily. A sharper version would ask the reply to test the cut against measured AI quality (reopens, escalations), not vendor deflection figures, before anyone is selected.

Consider an assertion that the reply turns HR's aim into something lawful, such as a union-agreed list on objective, role-based criteria fixed before scoring, instead of only rejecting it. Only some samples do this explicitly.

eval_feedback.overall: Passes all six. It is the only sample to name transition study support and to frame HR's aim through an agreed list, and its nine-step list is the densest. MBL comes third in the order, though 'now' covers it.
